programme: NCOR2 (SMRT) and HDAC3 form the core of the NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 corepressor complex, with MECP2 recruiting the same repressive machinery at a distinct but overlapping gene set: NCOR2 sits on nuclear-receptor and catecholamine-pathway loci (AR, RARA, ESR1, PPARD, NR2F2, NR1I2, and the tyrosine-hydroxylase gene TH), HDAC3 sits on vascular/angiogenic and inflammatory loci (VEGFA, MMP2, GATA2, CXCR4, TNF), and MECP2 sits on the cardiac/smooth-muscle differentiation module MEF2C-SRF-MYOCD plus NOTCH1. Together they read as a repressive complex gating both hormone-biosynthesis output and vascular/cardiac remodeling genes, rather than three unrelated regulons.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease, HDAC3 bound to NCoR/SMRT is a documented brake on vascular smooth-muscle and endothelial gene programmes (VEGFA, MMP2) and on the MEF2C-SRF-myocardin axis that MECP2's target list reflects; loss of this repression is a plausible route to pathological remodeling, but nothing in the retrieved record here places HDAC3/NCOR2/MECP2 specifically in Cardiovascular_Disease.
role_in_b: In pheochromocytoma, NCOR2's target TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is the rate-limiting enzyme of catecholamine synthesis in chromaffin cells, so corepressor control of TH and of adjacent nuclear-receptor targets (AR, RARA, ESR1) would set the tone of catecholamine output from the tumor; this is inferred from the target list, not from any disease-specific citation.
shared_axis: If the same NCOR2/HDAC3(-MECP2) corepressor complex loses its grip on TH in chromaffin tissue and on VEGFA/MEF2C-SRF-MYOCD in vascular tissue, the two diseases could be linked less through a shared tissue programme than through the tumor's hormonal output (catecholamine excess) driving the vascular phenotype — but this is a physiological, not regulatory-network, link, and it is our inference rather than a documented one.
reasoning: NCOR2 and HDAC3 are a real, well-characterized corepressor pair, and MECP2's target profile (MEF2C, SRF, MYOCD) is consistent with that complex's known substrates, so the module is nameable from the factors alone. But none of the three clears even 50% concordance (39, 39, 34 of 80), Open Targets shows no association for any of them in either disease, and the one retrieved paper touching a carrying factor is off-topic — so the account rests on general knowledge of the complex, not on anything placed here.
support: 22017809 - retrieved for NCOR2 alongside pheochromocytoma but its title/abstract concern spermatogenesis only, not the disease; no other retrieved paper confirms this programme in either disease.
how_to_falsify: ChIP for NCOR2 and HDAC3 at the TH promoter in pheochromocytoma/PC12 chromaffin cells to test whether the complex actually occupies and represses TH there, and separately test HDAC3 knockdown or NCoR/SMRT disruption in a vascular or cardiac model for de-repression of VEGFA/MMP2 and the MEF2C-SRF-MYOCD module; if occupancy or expression change is absent at either locus, the proposed shared corepressor axis does not hold.
caveats: The tissue pairing is adrenal (pheo) against blood (CVD), which are not directly comparable compartments, and the blood side already had its most obvious hematopoietic/erythroid regulators (KLF1, GFI1B, STAT5A/B, TFEC, IRF8) stripped out as tissue-generic — the surviving factors are what's left after that filter, not proof of a distinct causal programme. Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 80 patient-group comparisons, and the strongest carrying factor still recurs in barely half of them, well below the confidence implied by an example like 26/28. The single-view list (SND1, E2F1, HOXB6, HOXD8, TCF4, SOX1, FOXO4, SKI, SATB1, FOXP2, NFE2L3) shows several plausible-sounding candidates were dropped specifically because they came from one subgroup only, and none of them were used here.
